preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n, m, q, a_i, b_i, v_i ≤ 100000
Input format is correct: n, m on first line; m dislike pairs; q on next line; q salary revisions

preconditions.expression: all(a != b for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m] for a, b in [tuple(map(int, line.split()))])
preconditions.description: Each dislike pair (a_i, b_i) has distinct employees (a_i ≠ b_i)

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n for v in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2+m+i:2+m+q]])
preconditions.description: Each salary revision v_i is a valid employee index (1 ≤ v_i ≤ n)

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == [str(count_triples(salaries, dislikes)) for salaries, dislikes in zip([initial_salaries] + [update_salary(s, v) for s, v in zip([initial_salaries] + [update_salary(s, v) for s, v in zip([initial_salaries] + [update_salary(s, v) for s, v in zip([initial_salaries] + [update_salary(s, v) for s, v in zip([initial_salaries], [int(v) for v in stdin.splitlines()[2+m+i:2+m+q]]), i=0) for i in range(q))], [int(v) for v in stdin.splitlines()[2+m+i:2+m+q]]), i=0) for i in range(q))], [dislikes])]
postconditions.description: Output is a list of q+1 integers, where the i-th integer is the number of dangerous triples at the beginning of the i-th day (0-based index for initial state). A dangerous triple is a triple (a, b, c) where a dislikes b, b dislikes c, salary[a] > salary[b], and salary[b] > salary[c]. The initial salaries are [1, 2, ..., n], and each revision sets salary[v_i] = n + i to the highest salary, replacing any previous salary of v_i.
Output contains exactly q+1 integers (initial state + q days)
